transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marta Gomez (Sundial - Head of AI), Ethan Cole (Sundial - Infra Lead), Ravi Patel (Sundial - CFO)
Links shared: pricing-sheet (drive), security-pack (link), sample-bench-run-checklist (doc)

Auto-summary (auto):
Marta and team are evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for inference. Main constraints are monthly budget cap, P95 latency targets for user-facing chat, and data residency/KMS requirements for PHI. Discussed per-token hosted pricing vs amortized dedicated cost, batching and prefix/KV cache impact on unit economics, and pilot scope (benchmark + SSO + SOC2 docs).

Topics:
- Per-token pricing ballpark
- Batch and cache levers to reduce unit cost
- Dedicated amortization and reserved capacity commitments
- Private/VPC requirements for PHI and KMS integration
- Pilot plan and benchmarks

Action items (auto): see metadata action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (AE): All right, thanks everyone for joining. Um, quick intro from our side, I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood, and Priya our SE will run the perf bits.
[00:12] Marta: Hi, thanks, I'm Marta, head of AI at Sundial. We probably have like 40 minutes of content then Q/A.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan here, infra, I'll be the technical owner.
[00:19] Ravi: Ravi, finance, hoping to understand budget.
[00:22] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda — cost unit econ, hosting tradeoffs, pilot/next steps. Sound good?
[00:28] Marta: Yes. High level: we run a telehealth chatbot, roughly 250k monthly active users, but only a subset use the chat daily. We're budgeting $40k/month for inference right now — that's our hard cap.
[00:41] Jordan: Helpful. When you say inference, is that generation-heavy single-turn, or multi-turn with long context?
[00:46] Marta: Mostly multi-turn, average session 6 turns, often staying under 1k tokens per session, but some escalation flows hit 3k.
[00:53] Priya (SE): Got it. That mix matters for batching and KV cache benefits. If you have repeated system/prefix tokens we can get big savings via prefix caching — reduces token generation by reusing KV states.
[01:05] Ethan: Quick Q — our data is PHI, so we need KMS/HSM and VPC, and audit logs. Is that possible on hosted?
[01:12] Jordan: Short answer: hosted supports SOC 2 and customer-managed KMS for Private deployments; hosted can encrypt at rest and in transit but for strict PHI you often look at Dedicated or Private deployments with KMS integration and VPC peering. We can map that out.
[01:25] Ravi: From a cost perspective, what's the per-token ballpark on hosted? And what's the delta if we go dedicated?
[01:31] Jordan: Ballpark — for a production optimized model, hosted list could be around $0.00035 to $0.0005 per input+output token depending on model size and throughput. That's our public range; exact depends on model and SLA.
[01:44] Priya: On Dedicated, if you commit to reserved capacity, effective per-token cost can drop significantly — think in the realm of $0.00008 to $0.00018 per token after amortization, depending on utilization and batch sizes. Key levers: batching, continuous batching across requests, and KV/prefix cache hit rate.
[01:59] Marta: These ranges are wide. Can you give an example with our workload?
[02:03] Priya: Sure. Example: assume 10M tokens/day baseline for your active users, with an average of 800 tokens per session. On hosted at $0.0004/token that's $4k/day, which is obviously above your monthly budget. But with batching and 60% prefix cache hits we often see token generation drop and throughput improve — effective token-cost reduction of 40% or more.
[02:24] Ethan: Wait math check — 10M tokens/day times $0.0004 is $4,000/day equals 120k/month, yeah that lines up. So we need big reductions.
[02:33] Priya: Right — two knobs. First, batching: doing micro-batching at the runtime layer aggregates inference calls so GPU utilization goes up and per-token compute cost drops. Second, caching: for repeated system prompts or FAQs, prefix/KV caching eliminates regen for those tokens. In practice we see combined 50-70% unit cost reductions for chatty workloads with reuse.
[02:49] Jordan: Also routing — some lower-priority traffic can go to quantized lower-cost model variants, which reduces cost further while keeping quality for core flows.
[02:58] Ravi: And dedicated requires a monthly commitment — what's the break-even?
[03:02] Priya: Break-even depends on utilization. Rough rule: if you're above ~30-40% GPU utilization on reserved capacity for sustained period, Dedicated usually becomes cheaper. We'll run numbers in the spreadsheet.
[03:12] Marta: We have unpredictable spikes: morning rush and post-appointment windows, so burst capacity matters. How does Redwood handle spikes on Dedicated?
[03:21] Jordan: Dedicated supports autoscaling within reserved pools and burst into shared capacity for short bursts — can set policies. There's also a burst buffer add-on for predictable spikes. Fallback to hosted model variants is possible for excess requests.
[03:34] Ethan: For Private/on-prem: would we be managing the cluster? We're hybrid cloud today but some data must stay within our VPC.
[03:41] Priya: Private includes a customer-managed runtime in your VPC or on-prem, with Redwood control plane options. You handle networking and hardware, and we provide the inference runtime, optimizations, and support. That gives maximal control and KMS locality for PHI.
[03:54] Marta: Cost vs operational overhead tradeoff — we have limited infra SRE resources so dedicated hosted looks attractive if cost lines up.
[04:02] Ravi: Could you talk about how cache hit rate assumptions change the math?
[04:06] Priya: Absolutely. If you assume 0% cache hits — no reuse — it's pure compute. At 0% caching hosted $0.0004/token is baseline. At 50% caching effective token generation halves for new tokens, so your billed token volume halves (plus storage/requests overhead). With 60% caching+batching improvements with larger micro-batches you might get 60-70% effective unit cost reduction. We'll show scenario rows in the pricing sheet.
[04:30] Jordan: Note real world is mixed — some flows are single-use (clinical notes) and won't cache, others (system prompts, templated responses) are highly cachable.
[04:38] Ethan: Internally we do token compression pre-processing too — we sometimes strip stopwords for internal flows — curious if Redwood runtime would benefit.
[04:44] Priya: Preprocessing helps. Also we've got quantization paths — 4-bit runs can reduce GPU footprint and reduce cost for less latency-sensitive routes. But there's a quality tradeoff.
[04:54] Marta: On quality, we need to keep latency under 400ms P95 for core chat. Can you hit that with batching?
[05:00] Priya: Batching introduces queuing; if you tune max latency SLOs we continuously batch with small windows to preserve P95 targets. For 400ms P95, we typically set micro-batch windows at 10-25ms and use GPU-optimized kernels. If you need <200ms P95 it's tougher at larger batch sizes.
[05:15] Ethan: For the benchmark, can we measure P50/P95 and tokens/sec under our workload?
[05:19] Jordan: Yes, that's exactly the pilot: a 2-3 day benchmark where we run your traces through hosted/dedicated/private candidate configs and produce a per-token cost breakdown, latency percentiles, and recommended payload routing.
[05:31] Ravi: From finance POV, what's the commitment term for dedicated? Monthly/annual? 
[05:36] Jordan: We offer monthly reserved and annual reserved contracts. Annual offers lower unit pricing but requires a 12-month commit. There's also a trial reserved pool for pilot period.
[05:45] Marta: Any hidden fees? Data egress, logging, retention?
[05:49] Jordan: We bill compute and optional observability add-ons. Data egress is standard cloud provider charges in Private. For hosted, audit logs/long retention are add-ons. We'll put that in sheet.
[05:59] Ethan: Security review — do you have SOC2 and ISO?
[06:02] Jordan: Yes, SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 available; we'll share the compliance pack. For KMS we support customer-managed keys on Private and Dedicated.
[06:11] Marta: Great. Hypothetical numbers would help — can you put a worked example in the doc?
[06:15] Priya: We'll do that — sample rows: hosted baseline $0.0004/token, with 50% caching + batching effective $0.0002/token. Dedicated amortized might be $0.00009/token at 70% utilization. Private varies with your HW amortization.
[06:28] Ravi: If we assume monthly budget $40k, what's feasible?
[06:32] Priya: Roughly, at effective $0.00018/token you can do ~222M tokens/month. If your workload is 10M tokens/day that's 300M/month, so you need either higher caching or a bigger budget or mix of lower-cost models for non-critical traffic.
[06:47] Marta: So layering is key — critical flows on higher-quality model, others on quantized or smaller model. Routing policies then.
[06:54] Jordan: Exactly. We can set per-route model and quantization policies so quality-critical routes use full model in dedicated pool, low-priority hits quantized hosted variant.
[07:04] Ethan: For the pilot, what access do you need?
[07:07] Priya: Sample traces, schema for requests and average token counts, and a test service account with limited traces for benchmark. Optionally, SSH or cloud IAM for dedicated/private test cluster.
[07:16] Marta: We'll share traces (anonymized) and the SLO doc.
[07:20] Ravi: Timeline — when can we have the pricing sheet and pilot SOW?
[07:23] Jordan: I'll send initial pricing and SOW by Thursday, 2026-01-22. Priya will follow up with benchmark plan mid next week.
[07:31] Marta: Sounds good. A couple more clarifying questions...
[07:34] Ethan: Yeah — how do you measure cache hit rate? Do you instrument request tokens?
[07:38] Priya: Our runtime exposes cache metrics (prefix hit/miss, KV size) and we can instrument your traces to estimate expected hit rate pre-pilot. It's not perfect but gives a reasonable projection.
[07:48] Marta: Also curious about multi-tenant privacy on hosted — are requests co-located?
[07:52] Jordan: Hosted is multi-tenant at runtime but logical isolation and encryption; for strict tenant isolation or PHI you should evaluate Dedicated/Private.
[07:59] Ravi: Any penalties for scaling down reserved capacity?
[08:02] Jordan: We have flexible policies for reserved pools; the financials depend on contract. Monthly reserved can be adjusted with notice; annual is less flexible. We'll include options in the SOW.
[08:10] Marta: Ok, last thing — can Redwood handle model rollbacks if we see quality regressions after a change?
[08:15] Priya: Yes, we support rollouts, canary, A/B test, and automatic fallback to previous model variant on regression thresholds.
[08:23] Jordan: Quick recap of next steps: Jordan send pricing/SOW by 1/22; Priya schedule benchmark and checklist; Sundial to share traces and SLOs by 1/23. Any other asks?
[08:35] Ravi: Please include a row showing cost if we adopt 4-bit quantization for non-critical traffic.
[08:39] Priya: Will do.
[08:41] Marta: Thanks — that was helpful. We'll review the sheet and sync.
[08:45] Jordan: Great, we'll follow up. Thanks everyone.

[52:00] Meeting end (recording stopped)
